Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be an option to withdraw your question. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Investment Officer; David Wong, Head of Distribution; Emily Carter, Head of Operations; Robert Hayes, Head of Risk Management; and Anna Kowalski, Head of Technology.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by a combination of favorable market performance and robust net inflows that propelled our assets under management. Our AUM grew to $1.45 trillion, up 8% year-over-year and 4% sequentially, marking our 12th straight quarter of expansion. Equities led with gains from the S&P 500's rally fueled by cooling inflation and resilient earnings, adding significant lift to our equity franchise including active strategies and smart-beta ETFs. Fixed income faced some yield volatility but our active management provided alpha, while alternatives delivered uncorrelated returns from private credit and infrastructure. Net flows added strong organic growth, particularly from institutional channels and ETFs, outpacing peers amid client conviction in our multi-asset platform.

Michael Chen: Thank you, John. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $3.5 billion, representing a 25% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher average AUM, resilient fee rates, and inorganic contributions from strategic acquisitions. Our expenses were $2.2 billion, resulting in net income of $1.05 billion. Our expense ratio improved due to operational leverage and efficiencies from tech investments and M&A synergies.

Let me expand on that. Moving to our mergers and acquisitions activity, a key pillar of our inorganic growth strategy this quarter. In an industry with persistent fee compression to around 28 basis points for passive strategies per Morningstar, and shifts toward alternatives and ESG, we've pursued disciplined tuck-in deals to diversify products, enhance distribution, and scale AUM. Our focus remains on cultural fits, revenue synergies from cross-selling, and cost savings via shared infrastructure.

We closed two major transactions, accretive from day one, adding $14.2 billion in net new AUM, or 7% of our total $1.45 trillion. First, Horizon Sustainable Partners, a London boutique with $8.5 billion in ESG equity and fixed income, acquired for $450 million cash at 12x EBITDA—below the 15x average per PwC. It brings active ESG tools like their Climate Impact Scorecard with satellite and AI carbon modeling, fitting our sustainable suite now at $42 billion AUM, up 42% YoY versus global 31% per Bloomberg. Integration: 60% of $3.2 billion institutional mandates on our Aladdin platform, $12 million annual synergies. It strengthens Europe amid SFDR/CSRD, with Nordics/Benelux exposure for the €2.5 trillion EU pipeline per ESMA. Post-close flows: $450 million from US/APAC cross-sells.

Second, Pacific Rim Alternatives, Singapore-based with $5.7 billion in APAC private credit and real assets, for $320 million at 11.5x EBITDA. Boosts our alternatives to $38 billion, up 29% YoY, as clients seek yield in volatility. Their Pan-Asia Infrastructure Debt Fund at 9-11% net IRR complements us, tapping $5 trillion APAC alts by 2028 per Preqin. Phased integration via Synergy Engine unified systems, $8 million Year 1 synergies, 15% ops headcount cut. APAC now 18% of AUM from 12%, with Singapore for China QDII. Flows: $280 million from GIC/Temasek-like SWFs.

We also announced a 51% stake in Vertex Quant Strategies, $4.5 billion in low-vol/momentum ETFs, for $280 million, closing year-end, adding 50 bps to our 62 bps fee rate. Vertex's VERTX LVSM outperformed S&P Low Vol by 220 bps over five years, strengthening our ETF beta amid $8.1 trillion US ETF AUM per ICI.

Industry M&A hit $120 billion YTD, up 25% per Dealogic, as margins compress to 32%. We're selective for >15% organic growth. Pipeline: 5-7 LOIs in SMAs, LatAm FI, quant alts. KPIs: 92% retention, 15% cross-sell, 18% ROIC by Year 3. These offset $2.1 billion non-core outflows, targeting mid-teens AUM CAGR.

On compensation, our ratio was 42.3% for the quarter, down 180 bps YoY from 44.1% and 90 bps sequentially, as revenue outpaced comp amid talent investments. Comp expense $1.42 billion, up 9% on performance incentives; revenue up 18% on $1.2 trillion avg AUM. Fixed comp up 5% to $820 million with flat headcount at 4,200 via automation like ApexAI reducing recon by 35%. Variable up 14% to $600 million, 70% tied to 3-year outperformance—our equities beat peers by 120 bps per Morningstar. Deferred equity for PMs aids retention.

Regionally: Americas 41.5% ratio on ETF scale ($450B AUM); EMEA 45.2% for ESG talent; APAC 39.1% on PE revenue surge. Targeting 42-43% FY with $150M tech for margins to 32% in 2025.

Client retention was 95.8% FY to date, up 170 bps, top quartile per Coalition Greenwich. Institutional 97.2%, HNW 94.5% via SMAs, RIAs 95.1%. Driven by 82% 3-year outperformance, NPS 72, Client 360 AI preventing $2.5B outflows. New acquisition: $48.7B net inflows, 238 clients. ETFs $22.1B, active eq $15.8B, FI/SMAs $12.4B, alts $12.1B. Americas 72%, EMEA 18%, APAC 10%. Tech like Predictive Flows boosts conversions 18%.

Net flows by channel: $18.4B total, YTD $52.7B. Institutional $11.2B (61%), led by $2.5B pension, $1.8B SWF. Retail $4.1B (22%) via ETFs $2.9B. Alts $3.1B (17%), private credit $2.2B. Diversified for 12-15% growth.

Impact of markets and flows: Markets +$42B (3.4%), equities $35B, alts $12B. Flows +$28B organic. AUM to $1.45T.

Drivers: 68% AUM outperformed 1-yr, equities +320 bps, FI +45 bps. Trends: AI rally, alts yield.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by emphasizing quality beta, tactical tilts, and ESG integration to capture dispersion and trends like AI infrastructure. We launched the Apex AI Infrastructure ETF this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $3 billion in inflows reflecting demand for thematic exposure.

David Wong: Thank you, Lisa. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF and alternatives funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC and EMEA are paying off, as evidenced by 55% flow growth in APAC from partnerships with local platforms and sovereign mandates, plus UCITS ETF traction in Europe amid regulatory shifts.

Emily Carter: Thank you, David. Operationally, we've made significant progress in streamlining our middle and back office functions through cloud migrations and system unifications from recent deals. This has resulted in increased efficiency, reduced costs by 22%, and lowered operational risk. We are also focused on further automation to support SMA growth and tokenized assets.

Robert Hayes: Thank you, Emily. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and geopolitical exposures and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes advanced stress-testing with AI models achieving 88% drawdown prediction accuracy and quantum-resistant protocols.

Anna Kowalski: Thank you, Robert. On the technology front, we are investing in advanced analytics and AI to enhance our investment decision-making process and improve client service. We are also focused on strengthening our cybersecurity posture. Specifically, over three years we've committed $450 million to tech, 14% of OpEx, with $180 million this year split 65/35 capex/opex. Digital drove 28% retail AUM growth to $320 billion (22% total), 97% retention. ApexForge on AWS/Snowflake cut latency 60%, $45M savings; powers 1.2M SMAs. ApexGo robo onboarded 450K clients, 52% APAC adoption. AI/ML predicts drawdowns at 88%, gen AI for reports. $120M 2025 for blockchain/quantum. ROI 4.2x, margins +220 bps.

John Reynolds: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes guiding to Q4 net inflows of $22-27 billion, FY24 $75-85 billion for $1.35-1.42T AUM, FY25 $90-110B for $1.55T+, on 5-7% markets, Fed cuts, ETF/alts growth. Enablers: AI personalization, APAC/EMEA expansion, resilient fees.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. To ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Johnson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the recent M&A activity?

John Reynolds: Thanks, Mike. As Michael detailed, the Horizon and Pacific Rim deals added scale in ESG and APAC alts immediately accretive. Vertex pending will boost quants. Selective pipeline for high-growth fits.

Mike Johnson: Thank you. And a follow-up on the compensation ratio trajectory?

Michael Chen: Sure, Mike. At 42.3%, leverage from revenue growth and automation keeps us efficient versus peers. Expect 42-43% FY with tech efficiencies expanding margins.

Operator: Our next question comes from Susan Lee with JPMorgan.

Susan Lee: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the ESG Core fund?

Lisa Patel: Happy to, Susan. Our ESG suite, bolstered by Horizon, outperformed benchmarks by 150 bps, driving $450M post-close flows. Climate Scorecard integration enhances alpha.

Susan Lee: And how is the new product Apex AI Infrastructure ETF performing relative to expectations?

David Wong: Exceeding, Susan. $3B inflows already, tapping AI capex boom, with RIAs and retail embracing the thematic wrapper ahead of projections.

Operator: Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Morgan Stanley.

Alex Rivera: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Emily Carter: Absolutely, Alex. Cloud migrations and M&A integrations like Synergy Engine yielded $20M+ synergies, 15% headcount optimization, positioning for SMA scale.

Operator: Our next question comes from Karen Patel with Barclays.

Karen Patel: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Robert Hayes: Good question, Karen. SFDR/MiFID tailwinds boost ESG flows; we've enhanced monitoring with 95% STP and AI sentiment tools, maintaining low vulnerability.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Bradley with Citi.

Tom Bradley: How are you leveraging technology to improve investment performance?

Anna Kowalski: Tom, our ML models on 15-year data tilt for momentum/quality, 88% accuracy outperforming benchmarks. Gen AI and blockchain pilots next for tokenization.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to John Reynolds for closing remarks.

John Reynolds: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
